agentic.why: It is the live Yugos bfcl pool itself: same single-turn AST categories (simple/multiple/parallel/java/js/live/irrelevance/sql), same AST checker, ~30% no-call; F capped because it is a live set.

bfcl.overlap: is the live Yugos bfcl set: only the questions outside the live sample can be used, and never for testing
bfcl.summary: The 3,741 single-turn BFCL questions Yugos draws its 70 public agentic questions from (13 v4 AST categories = 3,641, plus 100 sql; 1,124 irrelevance/live_irrelevance = 30% expect no call; median prompt ~350 tokens with schemas). Per-question pass/fail is public for ~109 model configs (BFCL-Result score files list every failed id; newest Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2), so the rest of the pool is ideal router training data for agentic:public; scores top out near 0.83-0.85 because of label noise (Yugos field median 0.814), and no Nov-2026 model is on the board.
sources: local copy: /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/bfcl/bfcl_eval_data (question files, counts and token estimates)

math_code.why: different skill: multi-turn tool calling, not math or code writing

agentic.why: Multi-turn user requests (median 4-5 turns) over 8 simulated stateful APIs (file system, vehicle, trading, travel, messaging...), graded by executed state and response checks: close to the guessed private tau2-like shape, though without a simulated user; tool docs make inputs ~4-8k tokens.

1.model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Prompt), Multi Turn Acc (FC mode: 0.061 in 2025-08 snapshot)

3.model: Claude-Opus-4-5-20251101 (FC), Multi Turn Acc (Gemini-3-Pro-Preview FC 0.631; GPT-5.2 FC 0.281)

bfcl_multi_turn.summary: 800 multi-turn tool tasks (base, miss_func, miss_param, long_context: 200 each) on 8 simulated Python APIs, checked by the end state of the API objects plus the returned results after each turn. Same benchmark family as Yugos bfcl but none of these categories is in the Yugos pool; per-task pass/fail is public for ~109 model configs, and scores spread widely (Llama 8B 0.11, GPT-4o 0.43, Opus 4.5 0.68), so it is one of the best public stand-ins for hard private agentic questions.

chat.why: different skill: tool/function calling, not a question with a short answer

math_code.why: different skill: tool/function calling, not math or code writing

agentic.why: One user request solved by step-by-step calls (avg 3.26 steps / 5.07 calls) to Booking.com-style travel APIs with replayed real responses, scored by call matching against a golden path plus GPT-4o-judged final answer: a multi-step tool task close to the private guess, but single user turn and very long API outputs (needs 128k context).

complexfuncbench.summary: 1,000 complex function-calling samples (600 single-domain over hotels, flights, car rental, attractions; 400 cross-domain), each one user request needing several dependent calls with constraints and long parameter values. Real API responses are replayed when a call matches the golden one. A fresh (2025), verifiable stand-in for multi-step private agentic work in a booking domain like tau2 airline; per-model outputs are not published (the repo only saves your own runs). No late-2025 frontier score was found (OpenAI self-reported GPT-4o 0.665, GPT-4.1 0.655 on llm-stats).

chat.why: Short questions with one unambiguous exact answer (like simpleqa/hle), but most need web browsing, code or attached files to answer, so a tool-less one-shot answer is a different task.

math_code.why: different skill: web/file research questions, little math or code writing

agentic.why: Multi-step tool use (browser, code, file readers) graded by exact final answer, not by end state or call AST; no simulated user or business APIs; some questions need image/audio files.

3.model: GPT-5 Medium with HAL Generalist Agent, 165 validation questions (HF Open Deep Research scaffold: 0.628)

gaia.summary: 466 general-assistant questions in 3 levels (165 validation with public answers; test answers private), each with one short exact answer that needs web search, code and sometimes an attached image/audio/document. Gated: you must accept terms not to reshare it. Agent scores depend heavily on the scaffold (Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.75 vs 0.31 on HAL). HAL says it shares full, encrypted traces of its runs (32 validation runs of 2025 models); no GPT-4o or 2026 score was found. A weak stand-in for Yugos: the router sees text only, and these tasks need browsing.

chat.why: different skill: mostly function-calling chats; the plain-chat rows have free-form unverified replies

math_code.why: different skill: function calling, not math or code

agentic.why: Same core skill as bfcl (pick a function from JSON schemas and fill arguments, or decline when none fits), but rows are synthetic multi-turn chats (71% have more than one user turn in a 300-row sample) with invented function responses and unverified reference calls, mostly very easy single calls.

glaive_fc_v2.summary: 113k synthetic training chats: a system prompt with 0-2 JSON function definitions, then USER / ASSISTANT / FUNCTION RESPONSE turns with <functioncall> tags. In a 300-row sample, 32% had no functions and 52% contained a call, and the median length was ~420 tokens. Training data, not an eval: the answers are model-generated and unverified, there is no checker or difficulty spread, and it has been in many tool-tuning mixes since 2023. At most a source of easy bfcl-like prompts (incl. decline cases) after re-labelling.

chat.why: different skill: tool calls and JSON-schema outputs, not short-answer questions

math_code.why: different skill: tool calling / structured JSON, not math or code

agentic.why: func_calling_singleturn rows match the bfcl shape (tools in system prompt, one request, one or several parallel calls, ~1k tokens), func_calling adds tool responses; but the reference calls are synthetic and unverified, there are no no-call cases in the sample, and json_mode subsets are structured-output tasks rather than tool calls.

hermes_fc.summary: 11,578 synthetic training conversations in 5 subsets: func_calling_singleturn 1,893, func_calling 1,893 (with tool responses), glaive_func_calling 5,209 (Glaive-derived), json_mode_agentic 1,342, json_mode_singleturn 1,241. They use <tools>/<tool_call> tags across 63 business categories. The single-turn subset could supply bfcl-like parallel-call prompts, but the answers are unverified model output and there is no grader or score data. Freshness is middling (2024) and the set is widely used in training.

agentic.why: Realistic multi-step tasks over 28 live MCP servers (250 tools; 1-3 servers per task; gpt-5 averaged 79 calls), but graded by an o4-mini rubric judge plus schema checks rather than end state, live servers make outcomes drift, and contexts are far longer than Yugos's.

1.model: llama-3-1-8b-instruct, Overall Score (rubric average, not pass rate)

mcp_bench.summary: 104 tasks (56 single-server, 30 two-server, 18 three-server) synthesized by o4-mini and rewritten as fuzzy instructions, run against live MCP servers (finance, travel, science, academic search...). Scores are rubric averages from an LLM judge, not pass/fail, so they map only loosely to levels (guess_floor 0.2 is my allowance for easy schema points). Fresh and realistic, but small, long-context and not reproducible; no per-task results were found.

chat.why: About 20% are chat-type questions (43 HotpotQA, 76 MMLU) with exact answers, but they are asked as a multi-turn loop where the model runs Python tools and may get feedback.

math_code.why: 57% are math/code items (GSM8K 48, MATH 100, TheoremQA 49, HumanEval 45, MBPP 91) checked against ground truth/tests, but solved over up to 5 turns with a Python interpreter instead of one answer; old and partly from the MATH source of a live set.

agentic.why: Multi-turn tool use via executed Python code (and ALFWorld text actions, 134 items) graded by final answer, not JSON function schemas or end-state of business APIs.

1.model: gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, success rate at k=5 turns, tools, no feedback

2.model: gpt-4-0613 (2023 GPT-4; nearest to group 2), same setting

mint_bench.overlap: Contains 100 MATH and 43 HotpotQA problems, the source datasets of the live Yugos math and hotpotqa sets (whether these exact items are in the live samples is unknown); its 76 MMLU items are not MMLU-Pro.
mint_bench.summary: 586 items stratified from 8 older datasets (reasoning, code, ALFWorld) that the model solves in up to 5 turns by writing Python actions, optionally with GPT-4-simulated feedback. Per-instance results.jsonl exist for 55 old models (2023-24, e.g. gpt-4-0613, gpt-3.5, Llama-3-70B). Little value for Yugos: the underlying questions are old, available directly from their sources, and partly overlap live sets.

chat.why: different skill: output a sequence of tool calls, not a short answer

math_code.why: 76% are MathQA word problems, but the task is to express the solution as a chain of arithmetic tool calls, not to give a boxed answer.

agentic.why: Single prompt with JSON tool specs (pruned under 4k tokens) and the model outputs a nested call sequence where later calls use earlier outputs; graded by sequence match and by executing it (all calls executable). Same input shape as bfcl, but nested and math-heavy, with no no-call cases.

1.model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, win rate (executed answer correct), 3-shot direct; full-sequence accuracy 0.16

2.model: GPT-4o, win rate, 3-shot direct; full-sequence accuracy 0.28 (Llama-3.1-405B win rate 0.14)

nestful.summary: 1,861 nested API-call sequences: 1,415 from MathQA (40 math tools, avg 5.1 calls) and 446 coding-tool items from StarCoder2-Instruct (881+ tools, avg 2.1 calls), each with a gold sequence and a gold executed answer. It tests the dependent-call part of agentic work in bfcl's one-prompt format and is verifiable by execution. The domain is narrow (arithmetic tools), and no late-2025 scores or per-model outputs were found.

2.model: GPT-4-0613 (2023; nearest to group 2), overall Parameter F1

seal_tools.summary: 14,076 self-instruct instances over 4,076 ChatGPT-generated tools (4,076 single-tool, 10,000 multi-tool incl. 586 nested), built for agent tuning, plus an evaluation. The test-split size is not stated in what I read. A large, bfcl-shaped source of tool-selection prompts, but the labels are synthetic and unexecuted, and scores are F1s, not pass rates (gpt-3.5 0.68 vs GPT-4 0.73 param F1: little spread).

math_code.why: Python coding checked by hidden unit tests (FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS), but it is patching a whole repo from a GitHub issue over many tool steps, not writing one function from one prompt.

agentic.why: Multi-step agent work (bash/edit tools in a Docker repo) graded on end state by tests, matching the private guess in shape, but a software-engineering domain with no user conversation or business APIs and very long contexts; issues date from before 2024 and are heavily trained on.

swe_bench_verified.summary: 500 human-validated GitHub issue + gold patch pairs from popular Python repositories. Graded by running the repo's tests after the agent's patch. Per-instance resolved lists and logs are public for many submissions (SWE-bench/experiments plus submitters' repos). Useful mainly as a hard, end-state-graded agentic prior; its coding-agent domain and context length are far from Yugos's tool-calling questions. It is a Yugos catalog set, not in the live pack.

chat.why: different skill: repository bug fixing with tools, not a question with a short answer

math_code.why: Same as SWE-bench Verified (repo patching checked by tests) but only Django and Sphinx issues, so narrower Python domains.

agentic.why: Multi-step coding agent graded on end state by tests; same shape as the full Verified set but only 50 tasks from 2 repos.

level_guess.why: The card says the 50 were picked (k-means + linear programming, 16 models) to keep about the same performance, test pass rate and difficulty distribution as SWE-bench Verified. Copied from our row 11.1 measured scores (GPT-3.5 0.004; Claude 3.5 Sonnet/GPT-4o 0.511; GPT-5/Opus 4.5/Gemini 3 Pro 0.759). Level 4 is unknown, so it is set equal to level 3.

swe_bench_verified_mini.summary: A 50-task subset of SWE-bench Verified (Django and Sphinx only; ~5 GB of environments instead of 130 GB) chosen to match the full set's difficulty spread. Per-instance outcomes come from the Verified submissions, because these are the same instance ids. A cheap way to run a hard agentic prior, but too small and too far from Yugos's tool-calling questions to be much training data. It is a Yugos catalog set, not in the live pack.

taskbench.summary: 17,331 tool-automation requests on HF (daily-life APIs 4,318; Hugging Face model tools 7,458; multimedia tools 5,555; about the human-verified share of the 28,271 generated). Each is a single, chain or DAG of tool nodes with parameters. The daily-life API part is the closest to bfcl. The answers are plans graded by F1, not checked calls, it dates from 2023, and only GPT-4-era scores were found.

chat.why: different skill: customer-service tool conversation, not a question with a short answer

math_code.why: different skill: tool conversation, not math or code

agentic.why: A simulated customer talks to the agent, which follows a ~1.9k-token airline policy and calls a dozen booking tools (search, book, cancel, update flights/bags/passengers); graded on the final database state, required actions and communicated info. This is the shape we guess for private agentic, and tau2 retail/telecom/banking were Yugos's public agentic sets in v0.3.0.

tau2_airline.summary: 50 airline customer-service tasks (cancel, change or book under policy rules; 30 train / 20 test split) with a simulated user and end-state grading. A Yugos catalog set: tau2 retail/telecom/banking were in pack v0.3.0, airline never was. Per-task trajectories with reward and cost are public for 30 text submissions (up to Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, 2026-08) plus 16 legacy ones, which makes it one of the best sources for training the private-agentic route. Its only drawback is size.
